questions.question: Which executive system is present in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliamentary System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary System:**
 
• India follows a parliamentary system of government, which is derived from the Westminster model.
 
• In this system, the executive branch (the government) is responsible to the legislature (Parliament).
 
• The head of government is the Prime Minister, who is chosen from the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha (lower house of Parliament).
 
• The President is the head of state, but their role is largely ceremonial.
 
• The principle of collective responsibility is a key feature, meaning the cabinet is jointly responsible to Parliament.
 
• The executive derives its power from the legislative body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collegiate System:**
 
• A collegiate system involves a group of individuals sharing executive authority.
 
• This system is not employed in India's national government.
 
• It is more commonly found in organizations or smaller governing bodies.
 
• It is not a system of government in the way that the parliamentary and presidential systems are.
 
• This type of system is not a common form of national government.
 
• **Both Parliamentary and Presidential System:**
 
• India does not have a hybrid system that combines both parliamentary and presidential features.
 
• The Indian Constitution clearly establishes a parliamentary form of government.
 
• There are no elements of a presidential system incorporated into the structure of the Indian government.
 
• The Indian constitution is very clear in its description of a parliamentary system.
 
• The separation of powers works in a very different way in a presidential system.
 
• **Presidential System:**
 
• In a presidential system, the President is both the head of state and the head of government.
 
• The President is elected independently of the legislature and has a fixed term of office.
 
• There is a clear separation of powers between the executive and legislative branches.
 
• The United States is a prominent example of a presidential system.
 
• India's constitution does not allow for a presidential system of government.

questions.question: Which of the following states has bicameral (two houses) state legislature?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnataka** is one of the few states in India with a **bicameral legislature**, meaning it has two houses - the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** and the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).**
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** in Karnataka is the lower house, while the **Legislative Council** is the upper house.
 
• The system of bicameral legislatures in states is provided under **Article 169** of the **Indian Constitution**. It allows states to have a Legislative Council if the state legislature passes a resolution to that effect.
 
• The Legislative Council is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• Karnataka's Legislative Council plays a key role in reviewing and revising legislation passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Other Indian states with bicameral legislatures include **Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goa**__

 __
 
• **Goa** has a **unicameral legislature**, meaning it has only one house - the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).**
 
• The state does not have a Legislative Council.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**__
 __
 
• **West Bengal** also has a **unicameral legislature**, with only the **Legislative Assembly.**
 
• The state once had a Legislative Council, but it was abolished in **1969**.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**__
 
 
• **Punjab** has a **unicameral legislature** with only the **Legislative Assembly.**
 
• It does not have a Legislative Council.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, what is the tenure of the members of the State Legislative Council in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• State legislative council

 
 
• India has a bicameral system of legislature. Just as Parliament has two Houses, the states can also have a Legislative Council in addition to the Legislative Assembly through Article 169 of the Constitution.
 
• Six States having a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka.
 
• Recently, the Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Council has been abolished through the J&K Reorganisation Bill, 2019, which reduced the State of J&K to the Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh.
 
• Abolition or Creation - Article 169
 
• The Parliament can abolish a legislative council (where it already exists) or create it (where it does not exist) by a simple majority, that is, a majority of the members of each House present and voting, if the legislative assembly of the concerned state, by a special majority, passes a resolution to that effect.
 
• Special majority implies
 
• A majority of the total membership of the assembly and
 
• A majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of the assembly present and voting.
 
• Under Article 171 of the Constitution, the Legislative Council of a state shall not have more than one-third of the total strength of the State Assembly, and not less than 40 members.
 
• As the Rajya Sabha, the legislative council is a continuing chamber, that is, it is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution. The tenure of a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) is six years, with one-third of the members retiring every two years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• State Legislature

 
 
• Chapter III of Part VI of the Constitution is concerned with the State Legislature.
 
• It comprises state legislature and executives. 
 
• Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the organization, composition, duration, officers, procedures, privileges, powers, and so on of the state legislature.
 
• The Legislative Assembly
 
 
• It is the popularly elected chamber and is the real Centre of power in a State.
 
• The maximum strength of an assembly must not exceed 500 or its minimum strength fall below 60.
 
• But some of the States have been allowed to have smaller Legislative Assemblies, e.g. Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, etc.
 
• The territorial constituency demarcation should be done as far as possible, such that the ratio between the population of each constituency and the number of seats allotted to it is the same all over the State.
 
• Apart from these general provisions, there are also special provisions concerning the representation of SC and ST.
 
• The duration of the Legislative Assembly is five years.
 
• The Governor has the power to dissolve the Assembly even before the expiry of its term.
 
• According to 172 Legislative Assembly, is subject to dissolution. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
 
• The period of five years, may, while a proclamation of emergency is in operation, be extended by the Parliament by law for a period not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of six months after the proclamation has ceased to operate (Article 172(1)).

• He was designated as a senior advocate by the supreme court of India at age 34.

questions.question: Which Chapter of Part VI of the Indian Constitution is concerned with the State Legislatures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chapter III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chapter III** of Part VI of the **Indian Constitution** specifically deals with the **State Legislatures**.
 
• This chapter encompasses **Articles 168 to 212**, which outline the **structure, composition, and functioning** of the State Legislatures.
 
• It also includes provisions regarding the **Governor, Legislative Assembly, Legislative Council,** and their respective **powers and procedures**.
 
• Chapter III provides a framework for **law-making** at the state level, ensuring that the legislative process is systematic and consistent across different states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chapter II**__

 __
 
• **Chapter II** of Part VI deals with the **Executive** at the state level, focusing on the **Governor, his powers, and functions**.
 
• This chapter includes **Articles 153 to 167**.
 
 
 
• **Chapter V**__
 __
 
• **Chapter V** of Part VI pertains to the **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India**.
 
• This chapter includes **Articles 148 to 151** and outlines the **duties and powers** of the CAG.
 
 
 
• **Chapter VII**__
 
 
• **Chapter VII** of Part VI deals with the **States in Part B of the First Schedule**.
 
• This chapter includes **Articles 238**, which was repealed by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956.

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, every Legislative Assembly of every State, unless sooner dissolved, shall continue for _____ from the date appointed for its first meeting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• State Legislative Assembly​

 
 
• It is a Legislative body of the state.
 
• Subject to the provisions of Article 333, the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than five hundred, and not less than sixty, members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the State.
 
• Each State shall be divided into territorial constituencies.
 
• Members of the State Legislative Assembly, are elected directly by voting, from a set of candidates who stands in their respective constituencies.
 
 
 
• **​A Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) is a representative, elected by the voters of an electoral district (constituency) to the legislature of the State government in the Indian system of government.**
 
 
• From each constituency, the people elect one representative who then becomes a member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA). 
 
 
 
• Lok Sabha
 
 
• It is the lower house of the Indian Parliament.
 
• It is composed of representatives of the people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.
 
• 25 years is the minimum age for holding office in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The term of the members of Lok Sabha is a maximum of 5 years.
 
• Motions of no confidence against the government can be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
